matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value and compute the numeric difference between the two sides of the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving a matchstick puzzle, before considering any stick moves.
matchstick.example: Skipping the calculation of the numeric gap and moving a stick arbitrarily, which leads to a non‑equal equation.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Enumerate every way a single matchstick can be relocated from any character (including operators) to any other character, ensuring both source and destination remain valid symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the discrepancy, generate all candidate moves.
matchstick.example: Considering only moves that affect operators and ignoring viable numeral‑to‑numeral transformations such as V↔X.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, calculate how the numeric values of the affected numerals and operators change, and compare the total change to the required discrepancy.
matchstick.example: Choosing a stick move that changes a numeral by 2 when the required difference is 5, resulting in an incorrect equality.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A '+' consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick turns it into '-', and adding a vertical stick to '-' creates '+'.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the discrepancy suggests a sign change could resolve the equation.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical stick from '+' to make '-', but forgetting to adjust the arithmetic sign of the term.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If adding a stick to a numeral changes its value by the needed amount, move a stick from an operator (e.g., '-' or '=') to that numeral, ensuring the operator remains a valid symbol.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When no direct numeral‑to‑numeral transformation matches the discrepancy.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from '-' to a numeral and leaving '-' without any sticks, making it invalid.

matchstick.title: Equation structure preservation
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must still contain exactly one '=', each side must have at least one numeral, and all operators must be valid (+, -, =).
matchstick.when_to_apply: Throughout the transformation process, especially after each candidate move.
matchstick.example: Dropping the '-' sign and ending up with 'III = XII IV', which is not a proper equation.

matchstick.title: Known single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: Use a lookup of common single‑stick numeral changes (e.g., X↔V, I↔V, I↔X) and their associated numeric differences to quickly identify promising moves.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When matching the numeric discrepancy to a possible numeral change.
matchstick.example: Overlooking the V↔X transformation, missing the solution that changes IV to IX.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting Roman numerals
matchstick.principle: After any stick move, verify that each altered character still conforms to a standard Roman numeral representation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After applying a candidate transformation, before accepting it.
matchstick.example: Creating a shape with three diagonal sticks that does not correspond to any valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Maintain exactly one equality sign after stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from '=', ensure the source remains a valid operator (e.g., turning it into '-' if one horizontal stick is removed) and that exactly one '=' remains in the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is taken from or added to the equality sign.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal stick from '=', leaving only a single '-', thus losing the equality sign.

matchstick.title: Operator sign change impact
matchstick.principle: When a stick move changes an operator (e.g., '+' to '-'), account for the sign reversal of the term in the arithmetic evaluation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During numeric evaluation of candidate moves that alter operators.
matchstick.example: Changing '+' to '-' but still adding the term instead of subtracting it, causing the numeric check to fail.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model often moves a stick without checking whether the source or destination character still conforms to a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, verify that both the original and the modified characters are valid symbols before proceeding.

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may stop after finding a plausible‑looking transformation without checking the actual arithmetic result.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the numeric values of both sides of the equation after the move and confirm they are equal.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: When relocating a stick, the model sometimes removes an operator or numeral entirely, breaking the equation structure.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure the final equation still contains all required components: one '=', at least one numeral on each side, and any original operators (unless deliberately changed to another valid operator).

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: Changing '+' to '-' (or vice versa) flips the sign of a term, but the model may forget to adjust the arithmetic accordingly.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Re‑evaluate the expression with the new operator sign to see its effect on the total.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes adds or removes sticks instead of moving exactly one.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Track the source and destination of the single stick; ensure no extra sticks appear or disappear.
